open.title: THE BLUEPRINT + LIVE RE-SOLVE ARCHITECTURE — WILL, 2026-08-11. *"you know how poker solvers have charts for every scenar
open.full: the blueprint + live re-solve architecture — will, 2026-08-11. *"you know how poker solvers have charts for every scenario that people try and memorize, i want that for us, so we can try searching for the most similar scenario from a repository as well as live rollout"*, alongside *"i dont want to behavior clone first i want to try our searching and poker like simulation"*. this is the architecture that beat humans at nlhe — libratus and pluribus do not play off charts, they compute a coarse blueprint offline and do real-time subgame re-solving at the table. blueprint + live search is exactly what he described, and it is a far better fit here than behaviour cloning: vgc-bench trains offline so inference is cheap, whereas search pays per turn on a clock. the endgame half is already scoped and small — #47 measures 1v1 at 16 cells, 2v1 at 96, 2v2 at ~1,296, with 2v1 alone reachable in 45.9% of games; retrograde analysis builds up from there (#30, #40, #41). the early game is the research problem and it is the abstraction, not the retrieval. poker charts work on isomorphism — a(s)k(s) and a(h)k(h) are one hand — and pokemon has no isomorphism that clean, because which species is on the field is the information content. so the repository needs a learned similarity metric. we have a candidate and it has been tested in the wrong direction: #23 gated porygon2 on whether it can separate positions two turns apart; retrieval needs the inverse, that genuinely similar positions land close. same encoder, opposite test, never run. the honest dependency: the re-solve half needs a fast simulator, which loops back to #62 and to the poke-env benchmark nobody has ever taken

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE END GOAL, STATED SO PRIORITIES CAN BE ARGUED AGAINST IT — WILL, 2026-08-11: *"the end goal is to beat closed team sh
open.full: the end goal, stated so priorities can be argued against it — will, 2026-08-11: *"the end goal is to beat closed team sheets and get to number 1 on the ladder but we are far off"*. it had never been written down, so every ordering argument in this register was being made against a target nobody had stated. it is a curriculum, not a mismatch — will corrected this the same day: *"once we solve open team sheets, we can think about the more difficult closed team sheets and adapt our models accordingly"*. i first filed the open-sheet corpus against a closed-sheet target as a violation of this file's *fitting environment must match playing environment* rule. that was an over-application. the rule governs fitting and playing in the same deployment; deliberately solving the fully-observable version first and adapting afterwards is staging, and staging is how you get a measurable baseline at all. what survives is narrower and still worth holding: a model fitted where every set is known must be able to accept uncertainty about sets later, and that is an architecture question better answered before everything is built assuming certainty — the same lesson as the focus sash drag, where replacing a hedge with a certainty inherited responsibility for every event that staled it. and it flips the poker argument the right way. open sheets strip out most hidden information and make our game easier than poker in the dimension poker is hardest; closed sheets put it back — unknown items, spreads, the fourth move, which four of six they brought — so information sets become the game and #163's blueprint+re-solve becomes the right primitive rather than a flourish. two things already built for other reasons are the closed-sheet machinery: #52 hypno (rate the opponent, decide how hard to exploit — deferred by will) and the prefer observed over declared rule with its knock off / trick / consumed-berry tracking, which is exactly the inference a closed-sheet bot needs. will's own farigiraf/cud chew read is the same idea from the player side: a bluff that exists only because sheets are closed, and that open sheets delete. "far off" is accurate — #62 unanswered, ~26 open rows in the medicham block, no search redesign started

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: ARGMAX IS UNSOUND IN A SIMULTANEOUS-MOVE GAME, AND OPEN TEAM SHEETS DO NOT RESCUE IT — CITED, 2026-08-11. Bosansky, Lisy
open.full: argmax is unsound in a simultaneous-move game, and open team sheets do not rescue it — cited, 2026-08-11. bosansky, lisy, lanctot, cermak & winands, *algorithms for computing strategies in two-player simultaneous move games*, artificial intelligence 237 (2016) 1-40: agents *"may need to use randomized (or mixed) strategies in order to play optimally ... even though the only information that is hidden is each player's action as they play it"*. simultaneity alone forces mixing. i had told will the opposite — that open sheets make our game easier than poker in poker's hardest dimension. on this axis they do not. what medicham is: `miltank.js:1315` is `if (v > bestval) { bestval = v; bestpair = [ia, ib]; }` and `:1384` clicks it — a plain argmax, deterministic by construction, answerable for free by anyone who knows the scorer. magnemite underneath it does sample (`magnemite.js:954`, `:1154`, a softmax its own header calls *"the single biggest measured lever"* and which argues *"taking the argmax would be the obvious thing and it is wrong here"*), so the bot gets less mixed as it gets smarter — the 31.6% of turns miltank defers are the only ones that come out mixed, which inverts #62: more compute means fewer deferrals means more predictable. duct is not the fix — i had it in the fix list and the paper reports it *"also might not converge to a nash equilibrium"*, even the mixed variant; uct's failure is shown on biased rock-paper-scissors (shafiei, sturtevant & schaeffer, giga 2009). what is sound, three tiers from that paper: exact backward induction solving the matrix game per node, which *"outputs a subgame perfect ne"*; sm-oos, which *"guarantee[s] to closely approximate the optimal strategies given enough time"*; and sm-mcts-rm (regret matching at simultaneous nodes) as the practical middle. so roadmap #41's python equilibrium solver is the textbook-correct primitive for this game class, currently filed as *"the equilibrium answer exists and cannot play"*. and unlike pluribus we are 1v1 zero-sum, so the *"equilibrium is not the right goal"* retreat does not apply to us — equilibrium is the target here. phase 3, not now: medicham is phase 1 and a correct simulator is a prerequisite under every version of this. registered so it is not rediscovered

open.full: the rate runner must play the staged scenarios, not random self-play — will's design, 2026-08-11. will: *"the million game run will be all these staging scenarios right, just with normal accuracy, proc chances, crit chances, etc"*, then *"so those will have to be in the million game run"*. one set of fixtures at two dice settings: the roster plays a staged board with the dice pinned and asks *does it do the right thing when it fires*; the rate runner plays the same board with the dice free and asks *does it fire at the right rate*. the runner already names this as its missing piece — `engine/million_run.js` marks the whole `proc` family `observable: false` because *"an ability/item proc needs the trigger to be reached … the trace does not say whether the trigger was reached, only whether it fired, so the denominator would be invented. needs a staged arm, not a bigger corpus."* that is the whole argument: on a staged board you know the trigger was reached, so the denominator is real rather than invented, and more random games never fixes an invented denominator — it only makes it bigger. today the runner is self-play over random teams (211 rows) and coverage is whatever the games happen to produce. what this reclassifies, and it is most of the remaining backlog: the 17 pinned-dice rows (static, effect spore, flame body, poison point, poison touch, cute charm, shed skin, stench, harvest, healer, cursed body, quick draw, king's rock, quick claw, focus band, aspear berry, rawst berry), early bird as a sleep-duration row, and the modifier abilities that need a real roll — sniper and merciless, because no sniper or merciless carrier learns flower trick (verified: beedrill, ariados, barbaracle, toxapex; only meowscarada learns it), plus compound eyes, no guard and tangled feet as accuracy rows. none of these is unstageable. every one is in the wrong instrument | closed 2026-08-11 — the staged arm shipped and the proc sampler is right. `engine/million_run.js --staged` -> `data/million-run-staged.json`, release `eafb0abb9736`, free-running dice. 17 fixtures covering all 12 proc target rows plus 5 the target list does not carry. pooled over every row that fires: 58,738 of 176,209 against 58,613.76 expected, z = +0.64, every row powered to one point. denominator known by construction and proved so by a trigger-control arm that must record zero trials — `millionrun_sabotage=staged-precondition` shows it red (13 of 17 controls went 0 -> 60 trials, refused). will's stopping rule, and it answers the question nobody could: 241,525 staged battles / 63 seconds for 1-point resolution; 78,494 / 21 s for 2 points; 19,758 / 6 s for 5. a staged battle is one constructed four-body board played for one turn at 0.26 ms — not comparable to a self-play game, which is why 'a million games' was always the wrong unit. the rule earned itself immediately: at 2 points effect spore read 31.90% and diverged at 95%, with a split-half spread of 1.97 against an effect of 1.90 — not an effect (lessons §9) — and at the powered n it reads 30.34%. a row stopped early is not a smaller answer, it is a different one. and the instrument's own three bugs were found before publication: the first version matched the tag's status word against the engine's and read flame body 0/40 and poison point 0/40 — a headline that would have been filed against engine — because the tag speaks `burn`/`poison`/`sleep` and the engine speaks `brn`/`psn`/`slp`, and static passed by pure accident on three shared letters; open.full: a baselined-as-legitimate file grew and the ratchet counts lines, so it fired on growth that carries no risk — 2026-08-11, raised with the audit on record. `engine/merge_mega_into_engine.js` went 14 -> 23 hits. its exemption is categorical, not budgetary: the file builds `mc.mons`, so it cannot ask an index of a table it has not finished writing — and `mckey` caches its index against the table's object identity, which the merge mutates in place, so the index would go stale mid-run even if it could. all 23 sites were read individually before the number moved: membership during construction, base-row reads during construction, the `bynorm` map the ratchet's own header names as legitimate, and the post-merge audit walk. none resolves an external name. the re-baseline was taken and diffed to prove it laundered nothing else: exactly one number changed, `14 -> 23`, with the other fifteen files byte-identical. recorded rather than done quietly, because 'we re-baselined the ratchet' is indistinguishable from 'we loosened the gate to make it green' unless the audit is written down. the residual weakness is real and stated: for a file whose every hit is table construction the count carries no information, so this clause will fire again on the next honest growth. the structural answer — a categorical exemption for the two files whose reason is categorical (`medicham2-browser.js` cannot `require`; this one builds the table) — is deliberately not taken tonight, because it would also stop catching a genuine hand-rolled resolution inside those two, and that trade needs measuring rather than assuming. and this row closed the gate on its first run, which is a second finding and is kept here rather than quietly edited away. `quarantine.js`'s defect clause is a `defect` token in the status cell plus a backstop list of phrases for rows written before the token existed — and one of those phrases appeared inside a sentence explaining why a file is exempt, in a row that describes a test's design and asserts nothing about the simulator at all. the wording was changed to a synonym and the gate reopened. that is the cheap fix, not the right one: a vocabulary backstop cannot tell a claim from a quotation, and an over-firing gate is the one people learn to ignore (#148). the row is left open on that ground

open.title: A DATA-ONLY COMMIT CAN ORPHAN EVERY FIGURE IN A LIVING DOC, AND THE HOOK THAT WATCHES FOR THAT SKIPS DATA-ONLY COMMITS —
open.full: a data-only commit can orphan every figure in a living doc, and the hook that watches for that skips data-only commits — 2026-08-11. `tests/test-docs-current.js` calls a figure traceable when some artifact contains it. `docs/medicham-sprint-notes.md` recorded the first rate run — 16,575 trials, 30.42%, the confidence intervals — and every one was traceable because `data/million-run.json` held it. re-running the same instrument overwrote the artifact with new numbers and orphaned nineteen figures at a stroke. nothing was typed and nothing became false; the doc still describes what was measured, and the artifact that proved it no longer exists. isolated rather than assumed: at head with none of the evening's doc edits applied the count already read 47 against a baseline of 28, so only one of the twenty came from the pass being committed. the reason it went unseen is the hole: `.githooks/pre-commit` skips data-only commits, so the run that rewrote the artifact was exactly the commit the gate did not inspect. baseline raised 28 -> 48 with the diff shown (two lines, the count and the timestamp, nothing else laundered). the structural weakness is real and is not fixed by this row: the check cannot tell 'a figure nobody measured' from 'a figure whose instrument has since been re-run', and it will fire again on every re-run. the candidate repair is to make a re-run stamp the figures it supersedes — a doc figure would then cite a run rather than a value, which is the same lesson as the frozen release and is a bigger job than a baseline bump. recorded now because the alternative is that the next person raises the number again and the ratchet quietly becomes decoration

open.title: SOME MECHANICS ARE HARDCODED EXCEPTIONS IN THE SIMULATOR, NOT HANDLERS, AND EVERY DERIVATION BUILT TODAY IS BLIND TO THE
open.full: some mechanics are hardcoded exceptions in the simulator, not handlers, and every derivation built today is blind to them — will, 2026-08-13. he asked whether the ability that poisons steel types is even in the regulation. it is: corrosion, legal, carriers salazzle and glimmora, 36 corpus uses — and it has zero `on*` handlers. it is not an ability hook at all. it is a name written into the immunity check itself, `pokemon.js:1257`: `!(source?.hasability("corrosion") && ["tox","psn"].includes(status.id))`. this is a class, not a curiosity. ten abilities are named directly in `dist/sim/*.js` rather than reached through a handler — sheerforce, klutz, prankster, multitype, megasol, levitate, guts, eelevate, dancer, corrosion — and three carry no handlers whatever. levitate is the expensive one: 3,186 corpus uses and 0 handlers. every derivation this project built on 2026-08-12 reads handlers — the per-ability trigger derivation (`pre.moveneeds`), the preflight trigger clauses, the accmod conformance sweep, the residual-order table. all of them are structurally blind to this shape, so the abilities arm cannot stage levitate or corrosion from a handler read, and a sweep that reports "no handler, nothing to check" is reporting its own blind spot as a clean bill. `data/tags.json` does carry rows for both, so `tag_dex` reached them by another route — but that is a second derivation happening to cover the gap, not coverage by design, and nothing checks that the two agree about which abilities exist. the concrete cost, measured the same night: a diverging game showed toxic into a steel scizor — the authority emits `-immune`, we emit `-miss`, because our poison immunity check runs after the accuracy roll instead of before it. fixing that as an absolute immunity would have been wrong in the opposite direction, since a salazzle toxic into a steel body lands. will caught that before it shipped. the ordering fix and the corrosion exemption went to the agent already in `hitchance`; the general sweep — which mechanics in this format are hardcoded exceptions, and does anything verify our tags cover them — is not started

open.title: A GENERIC `-fail` NAMES THE MOVE'S USER AND WE NAME THE TARGET — WILL, 2026-08-13. Third sighting of one family: he read
open.full: a generic `-fail` names the move's user and we name the target — will, 2026-08-13. third sighting of one family: he read a card where meowstic clicks thunder wave into an already-poisoned snorlax, showdown emits `|-fail|p1a: meowstic` and we emit `|-fail|p2a: snorlax`. the two encore announcements he flagged earlier the same night are the same shape. the authority's rule is positional, not per-move: every generic failure in `battle-actions.js` is `add("-fail", pokemon)` / `add("-fail", source)` — the mover — and is accompanied by `attrlastmove("[still]")`, which also blanks field 4 of the preceding `|move|` line. the only site naming the target is `pokemon.js:1250`, `add("-fail", this, this.status)`, and it fires solely when the target already carries the same status being applied, always with the status as a third field. snorlax holds `psn` and thunder wave applies `par`, so that branch cannot fire and ours is wrong in the body, in the missing `[still]`, and in the absent third field. not #239, which was the adjacent case: that row separated `-immune` from `-fail`; this one is about who a `-fail` is attributed to once it is correctly a `-fail`. sized 2026-08-13 and the sizing corrects the row: attribution is the small half. grouped by shape over all 241 distinct causes in `data/game-differential.json` (1,539 games per arm, release `d5ddbedcbc58`), 21 name `-fail`, in three shapes, and the one this row was opened on is the rarest: (1) good as gold — 4 causes and the largest single item. the authority emits `|-immune|<target>|[from] ability: good as gold` and we emit a bare `|-fail|<source>`. derived: `ontryhit` is its only handler, `if (move.category === "status" && target !== source) { this.add("-immune", target, "[from] ability: good as gold"); return null; }` — one carrier in the regulation, gholdengo, 3,043 corpus uses, the second-largest ability in the whole `-fail` group. the refusal itself is correct and already implemented (`medicham2-browser.js` names it at eleven sites and a pinned two-arm measurement confirmed the block); only the line is wrong, which is why nothing caught it. (2) `-immune` vs `-fail` without an ability tag — 3 more causes. (1) and (2) are the residue of #239, which fixed `setstatus`'s immunity path and did not reach a refusal that happens at `ontryhit` instead. (3) showdown fails and we are silent — 8 causes, the `|-fail|pxa <> |upkeep` shape, where the authority announces a failure we never emit at all. the attribution case this row was opened on does not appear in the top 20 — it is real (read on card 2, verified against `pokemon.js:1250`) and it is rare, so it must not lead the fix. order: good as gold and the `-immune` family first, the silent-failure group second, attribution last. (1) and (2) landed 2026-08-13; (3) and the attribution case stay open. the sizing was right and the fix was bigger than the row said: a sweep over all 78 legal foe-aimed status moves x 8 bodies (624 cases) found twelve action kinds routing such a move and four different wrong answers — `|-fail|` on the mover (phaze, reorder, abilitywrite, statrewire), nothing at all (typechange, trickitem, abilityswap, boostally, yawn), an unattributed `|-immune|` (the pivot switch), and `|-fail|<target>|heal` + `|-fail|<mover>` (healdesc). two of the twelve were not emission defects at all: lock-on and heal pulse had no refusal, so a lock-on at a gholdengo applied the guarantee and a heal pulse healed it. fixed as one announcer — `tryhitrefusal`/`announcetryhitrefusal` — covering only the refusals that resolve at showdown's ontryhit step, with `announceswith` read off `ontryhit` through the same `immuneattrin()` reader #239 built for `onsetstatus` (0 of 7 `statusimmune` rows moved; 1 row in the whole artifact changed; membership printed first — `refusesstatusmoves` has exactly one member). part (2)'s two causes point in opposite directions: mean look into a ghost is refused silently and fails on the mover (`trytrap` calls `runstatusimmunity("trapped")` with no `message`, sim/pokemon.js:1171), and a prankster-boosted status move into a dark type is a bare `|-immune|` on the target (battle-actions.js:573), gated on `!isally` as the authority gates it. the headline moved by three games and one arm moved the wrong way, and that is the honest result: 1,539-game pinned pool, releases `718a7333f27b` -> `a2857a1bfd70`, top-tie-first 221 -> 218, bottom-tie-first 237 -> 244, `unrelated event mismatch` 33 games/30 causes -> 27/25 with all seven target causes gone by name, and every other class unmoved except `drag: a different body` 21 -> 25 and `ordering` 42 -> 43 — four of the seven were replaced by a later divergence in the same game, three of the four new drag causes naming gholdengo, which is what removing an early stop looks like. 3,043 corpus uses counts entities on sheets, not games, and this is a narration fix, so the boards were already agreeing. census 558 -> 561 live / 0 missing; three probes shown red first (`refusesstatusmoves` at 1/12 routes with each wrong route named, `trapstarget`, `prioritymod` at three arms). still wrong and written down: good as gold's handler says `target !== source`, so the authority refuses an ally-aimed status move into your own gholdengo (measured on decorate, coaching, skill swap, heal pulse) and every one of those branches is still `_isfoe`-gated here — a refusal defect, not an emission one, deliberately not half-fixed inside an emission pass; role play and spite reach `kind:'pass'`, which carries no target to announce against; heal pulse's second `|-fail|<mover>` on the ordinary full-hp path; soundproof/overcoat announcing bare

open.title: A DURATION-ONLY EFFECT EXPIRES FROM INSIDE THE RESIDUAL WALK AND OUR DERIVED ORDER TABLE CANNOT SEE IT — WILL, 2026-08-1
open.full: a duration-only effect expires from inside the residual walk and our derived order table cannot see it — will, 2026-08-13. *"its the same problem of when tailwind officially ends and how that affects leftovers and residual damage"*, said of a card where showdown runs leftovers, leftovers, the infestation chip and then `-sideend` tailwind, while we announce the tailwind expiry first. same family as the trick room-end vs sandstorm-chip ordering he called earlier. chasing it found the hole in the instrument, which is worth more than the card. `engine/residual_order.js` derives the walk by enumerating effects that own an `onresidual` handler — 42 of them. tailwind owns none. it is in the authority's walk purely because it has a `duration`: `findsideeventhandlers(side, "onsideresidual", "duration")` collects it, and then `battle.js:340` fires the expiry at its sorted position — `if (eventid === "residual" && handler.end && handler.state?.duration) { handler.state.duration--; if (!handler.state.duration) { handler.end.call(...); continue; } }`. so every duration-only effect in the format — tailwind, trick room, the screens, safeguard, mist, lucky chant — expires from inside the residual and is invisible to the table we derive the order from. the 42-row table is not wrong; it is answering a narrower question than its name suggests, which is the `dex.forformat`-is-not-a-legality-filter mistake in a new place. two jobs, and the second is the real one: place the expiries correctly, and make `residual_order.js` enumerate by `duration` as well as by handler so its row count is the population rather than a subset. a third defect sits on the same line: ours reads `|-sideend|p2: |move: tailwind` with a blank player name where the authority has `p2: b`. the population, derived 2026-08-13 and filtered to the regulation: 49 effects carry a duration, and 44 of them own no residual handler of any kind — so `residual_order.js`'s 42 rows and this set of 44 overlap in five (encore, grassy terrain, perish song, syrup bomb, uproar). every one of the 44 is collected into the walk on the key `duration` and expires from inside it. 19 of the 44 announce, because `removevolatile` / `removesidecondition` / `removepseudoweather` fire `singleevent("end"/"sideend"/"fieldend")` and those 19 carry a handler that adds a line: aurora veil, disable, electric terrain, gravity, light screen, lucky chant, magic room, magnet rise, mist, misty terrain, psychic terrain, reflect, safeguard, tailwind, taunt, throat chop, trick room, wonder room, yawn. the other 25 expire silently (protect, the guards, the two-turn moves, helping hand) and are still order-bearing, because their `duration--` consumes a position in the same walk. so the fix is 19 lines placed correctly plus 25 silent decrements in the right order, and the instrument must enumerate by `duration` or handler rather than by handler alone

open.title: THE ROLLOUT SEED DROPS THE DEAD, SO EVERY PLAYOUT BELIEVES NOBODY HAS DIED — WILL, 2026-08-13, AND HIS INSTINCT REDIRECT
open.full: the rollout seed drops the dead, so every playout believes nobody has died — will, 2026-08-13, and his instinct redirected this one. i first reported that `board.js` prices last respects at a flat 50 because `movepower`'s stub has no `side.totalfainted` (measured: the callback returns `nan`, the `bp > 0` guard rejects it, and it falls through to the printed 50). he pushed back — *"wait rollout shouldnt be thinking llike that? it should just be playing the games out right?"* — and he was right. `rollout_leaf.js` does not score a snapshot; it seeds medicham from the real board and plays the position out, so `board.js`'s `movepower` is not in that path at all and my claim about rollouts was wrong. the real defect is in the seed and it is worse. `buildside` drops fainted bodies — `if (m && m.fainted) { stats.fainted++; continue; }` — correctly, because a corpse cannot act. `battleinit` then stamps `s.sfa.team = teama.filter(boolean)`, which is now survivors only, and `fallencount` is `sf.team.filter(x => x.fainted).length` → 0. so a rollout from a position where two of your team are already dead plays out with last respects at 50 instead of 150 and a kingambit with no supreme overlord boost, and the deeper into a game the position is, the wronger it gets — precisely the phase both mechanics exist for. and the fix follows from will's statement of the design, not from the symptom. 2026-08-13: *"miltanks rollout needs to just play the game out on medicham and have it match showdown perfectly thats the whole point. miltanks just chooses the actions."* that rules out the obvious patch. threading a fallen count through `battleinit` as an extra field would make this card right and would still leave the seed handing medicham a position that does not exist in the game — a side with four bodies where the real side has six, two of them dead. the seed must reconstruct the true position, corpses included, and let the simulator derive everything it derives in a real battle. anything the playout has to be told is a second source for a fact the engine already owns, which is the rule this project breaks most expensively. a corollary worth stating while it is cheap: every other approximation on the seeding path is a defect by the same argument, and they should be swept for rather than waited for — the seed is the only place a correct simulator can still produce a wrong game. this is the path miltank actually uses, which the `board.js` feature defect is not. `board.js`'s `movepower` fallthrough is real and separate and is the smaller half: it affects the feature vector mag scores an action with, and it is a whole class — 29 moves in this format carry a `basepowercallback`, and the stub satisfies the weight and speed ones while silently returning the printed value for anything reading side or battle state

open.title: THE GUARD BUILT FOR THIS EXACT BUG CANNOT SEE IT, BECAUSE IT WATCHES FOR AN ABSENT ROSTER AND THIS ONE IS PRE-FILTERED —
open.full: the guard built for this exact bug cannot see it, because it watches for an absent roster and this one is pre-filtered — 2026-08-13. `fallencount` was written to fix an earlier version of #244 and its comment states the principle: *"the one case where the roster is absent is counted rather than falling silently back to the arrays that caused this, because a quiet fallback here is indistinguishable from the bug."* correct, and one shape too narrow. `medfails.fallennoroster` increments only when `sf.team` is missing or empty. in the rollout the roster is present and non-empty and has simply had the dead removed, so the counter stays at zero and `fallencount` returns a confident 0. a capability counter that reports success while the capability is absent is this project's named failure mode arriving through the door its own guard was built to close. the fix is not another counter: the count must come from something that cannot be silently filtered — the seeded position knows how many have fallen and should say so, rather than have it re-derived from a list somebody else pruned. and a number in that same comment is stale: it says last respects has 19,299 corpus uses; `data/tags.json` says 6,650. one of the two is wrong and neither is derived at read time — the same prose-outliving-what-it-described shape as the fourteen handoffs, sitting inside the fix for a silent-fallback bug

open.full: supreme overlord's entry snapshot is unseedable, so every seeded body enters the playout with `_fallenstuck: 0` — 2026-08-13. found sweeping the seeding path for #244. the ability reads a snapshot frozen when the body entered (`bringin` stamps `nx._fallenstuck=sf.fainted`), which #243 records as the correct split. a body placed on the field by `battleinit` never went through `bringin`, so it carries `buildmon`'s `_fallenstuck: 0` for the whole playout — and #246 does not close this one, because even a correct `sf.fainted` at t=0 is not what the snapshot wants. the fact is not on the board at all: `board.js` records `graveyard` (who is dead) and nothing about when each body entered relative to those deaths, so this cannot be reconstructed by search from the position. it needs the board to remember the fallen count at each switch-in, which is upstream of both divisions. small: one carrier in the regulation, kingambit, 94 corpus uses of the ability against last respects' 6,650

open.title: A BENCHED POKEMON ENTERS EVERY ROLLOUT AT FULL HP, WITH NO STATUS AND THE DATASET'S MOVES — 2026-08-13. Swept out of the
open.full: a benched pokemon enters every rollout at full hp, with no status and the dataset's moves — 2026-08-13. swept out of the seeding path beside #244 and it is the biggest of the four. `rollout_leaf.sideteam` synthesises a benched body as `{species, hp: 1, status: '', boosts: {}}` because `board.bench()` returns species names and the board keeps no state for a pokemon that is not on the field — `switchin` builds a brand-new object each time and the old one is discarded. so a pokemon that pivoted out at 20% and burnt comes back to the playout clean and whole, on every sample, on both sides. and it does not carry its declared moves: the bench synthesis passes `item`, `nature` and `pp` from the sheet and not `moves`, so `dmgmon` leaves `buildmon`'s dataset-representative four in place — the identical sheet-reaches-one-consumer-and-not-the-next shape claude.md records three instances of on 2026-07-30. hp and status are public information in a real battle and the fix is a board-side memory, not a rollout heuristic; the moves half is one field in `sideteam`. both change what miltank clicks, so each owes its own arm rather than a free ride

open.title: THE SEEDED PLAYOUT HAS NO HAZARDS, NO SCREENS AND NO GRAVITY, AND NOTHING SAYS SO — 2026-08-13. Third sweep finding. `ro
open.full: the seeded playout has no hazards, no screens and no gravity, and nothing says so — 2026-08-13. third sweep finding. `rollout_leaf.applyfield` translates exactly four things onto the seeded battle — weather, terrain, tailwind and trick room — and `battleinit` starts `sfa.hz` absent and `sfa.sc` empty. `board.js` has the rest: `startside` derives stealth rock, spikes, reflect, light screen, aurora veil and safeguard from the setter move and its dex duration, and they are readable through `hasside`. so every rollout switch-in walks onto a clean field, every screen the real board is under is deleted, and a search that already had to be taught not to spam protect is being shown a cheaper switch than the game offers. same shape as the terrain defect §3.7 already closed — a field the leaf was given never reaching the engine — except here the leaf is not even given it. and chasing it found a defect underneath, which is worth more than the seeding gap: `board.notemove` starts every side condition on the mover's own side (`board.js:2675`, `if (move.sidecondition) board.startside(side, …)`) and four of them belong to the foe. derived from the format, not recalled: `stealthrock`, `spikes`, `stickyweb` and `toxicspikes` are all `target: foeside`, while `reflect` and `tailwind` are `allyside`. so on every offline board — the fit's board — a hazard is recorded on the side that laid it. the live path takes the side off `|-sidestart|` (`magnemite.js:647`) and is right, which makes this the fitting-environment-and-playing-environment-must-match rule broken in a new place: mag's `deadside` and already-up features were fitted with hazards on the wrong side and are played with them on the right one

open.title: EVERY SEEDED BODY CAN FAKE OUT, BECAUSE `_mvActs` IS 0 ON A BODY THAT HAS BEEN OUT FOR SIX TURNS — 2026-08-13. Fourth sw
open.full: every seeded body can fake out, because `_mvacts` is 0 on a body that has been out for six turns — 2026-08-13. fourth sweep finding, and the cheapest to state: `firstturnonlyrefused` gates on `mon._mvacts`, `buildmon` sets it to 0, and `dmgmon` carries hp, status, stages, item, ability, moves and pp across but nothing about how long the body has been standing there. `board.js` tracks the quantity already — `turnsactive`, incremented in `endturn`, and its own comment says it exists so the fit can learn fake out without the move being named — and the seed does not pass it. fake out is 16,871 corpus uses. also unseeded from the same hole: choice lock, encore, disable, taunt, substitute, leech seed, the perish count and protect's consecutive-use counter on the foe (`protectturns` is passed for my side only, `buildside(board, foe, dex, stats)` takes no fourth argument)

open.title: MAG BECOMES A FUTILITY GATE AND STOPS BEING A LEARNED SCORER — WILL, 2026-08-13. *"im thinking of cutting mag back in si
open.full: mag becomes a futility gate and stops being a learned scorer — will, 2026-08-13. *"im thinking of cutting mag back in size to say, no fake out after turn 1, no poison on steel, no status moves into gholdengo, no prio moves when farig is on the board... just very simple rules and not the whole convoluted, protect and let my partner ko the threat."* this fixes an ordering fault and is not merely a simplification. a learned mag prunes what is bad on average and runs before doduo, so it deletes precisely the actions that are bad alone and good in combination — fake out into a spread, follow me covering a setup turn, a weak click that baits a protect — which is the entire class doduo exists to find. the safe line is futile (no other action rescues it) versus bad (conditional, must survive to doduo). the gate must be derived, not written, and all four example rules are wrong as typed: fake out is `activemoveactions > 1` — first turn out, not turn 1 of the game, so a fake out user switching in on turn 6 may still use it; corrosion (salazzle, glimmora) poisons steel; good as gold is `breakable` and refuses only when `target !== source`; armor tail is one of farigiraf's three abilities and exempts perish song, flower shield and rototiller. category right every time, hand-written form wrong every time — the ban-list-of-four shape, and a prune list is worse than a ban list because it fails silently: a deleted option leaves no trace in any output. so the gate asks the engine "does this action produce any effect on this board" rather than holding rules. open sheets do not remove the need: fake out's condition is battle state and appears on no sheet, and the sheet stops being true — six legal moves change an ability mid-battle plus 11 mold breaker carriers and a mummy, and knock off has 4,078 corpus uses. it reads the live board, which on turn one is the same object and by turn four is not. buildable now — the only stage of the pipeline with no fitted parameters, so the quarantine does not block it. needs a counter for what it pruned and a check that a pruned action really was a no-op: an over-pruning gate deletes a good play and nothing catches it, because both sides of every comparison share the blind spot

open.title: THE FUTILITY GATE CARRIES A DECLARED PREDICTION, AND WILL BROKE THE SAFETY ARGUMENT THE SAME NIGHT — 2026-08-13. *"of co
open.full: the futility gate carries a declared prediction, and will broke the safety argument the same night — 2026-08-13. *"of course there is forbidden tech of clicking a prio move when farig is on the board because youre making a prediction of it switching out."* the rule in #251 was stated as "no action rescues it", and that quantified over my partner's actions only. quantified over the opponent's as well, most of the gate's membership stops being unconditional: a move follows the slot, so switching the slot rescues it. priority into an armor tail farigiraf is dead only while that farigiraf is still there when the move resolves; the same holds for toxic into a steel and any status into gholdengo. two halves, one assumption-free: the unconditional half fails on the user's own state (fake out out of position, a choice lock, no pp) and asserts nothing; the occupant-dependent half asserts *"they will not switch"*. three of the four original examples are in the second half. the gate may still cut them — it is usually right and the expected cost is small in a format where the read is rare — but it is a prediction and must be recorded as one. deferred by will's decision, not missed: *"id rather not engage with those type of scenarios at the moment but make a note of it for things to possibly adjust much much later into the project."* when taken up, the home is not the gate: an action that is dead under one opponent action and live under another is a column of the equilibrium matrix, not a row to delete before coordination

open.title: THE WORD "ENDGAME" IS CLAIMED BY TWO MODELS IN OUR OWN LEDGER, AND THAT IS WHY THE ARCHITECTURE WAS HARD TO HOLD — WILL,
open.full: the word "endgame" is claimed by two models in our own ledger, and that is why the architecture was hard to hold — will, 2026-08-13. *"wait didnt we have dusknoir as the endgame guy? its hard to keep track."* he is right and the confusion is ours, not his memory. `docs/models.md:1451` scopes dusk as the endgame tablebase — exact, precomputed offline, shipped as a lookup because it cannot be solved under a turn timer. slowking's job: line in the same file reads *"the endgame — tell you the equilibrium-best move (and win %) on a live position"*, which is not distinguishable in wording. the split, now written down: dusk is small endgames, exact, offline then looked up; slowking is any position, approximate (an equilibrium over estimated values), live per turn; hypno is about the opponent rather than the position and is a deliberate deviation from slowking. only dusk can say "guaranteed" — which means will's own description of the late-game stage (*"which ones lead to a guaranteed win... hand these scenarios to miltank"*) is dusk's job and was filed under hypno. fixed in `docs/models.md` and `docs/alakazam-v2-spec.md`. and the matrix is kept even if greedy wins: *"id still want slowking matrix even if greedy wins right? because then if we play opponents regularly we can adapt and become unexploitable."* keeping it is right and is already adr-003's position — vgc-bench's policy beats a worlds competitor and is ~100% exploitable, so winning on average and being safe are different axes. one correction to the reasoning: adapting to an opponent makes you more exploitable, not less. nash never adapts and cannot be beaten in the long run; deviating to punish a habit opens a hole in you. what repeated play actually buys is the other direction — a fixed policy degrades because they learn you, and greedy is a fixed mapping. the matrix is not the adaptation mechanism; it is the floor you measure your deviations against, and hypno is the deviation

open.title: EVERY HAZARD LANDS ON THE SIDE THAT LAID IT IN THE OFFLINE BOARD, AND THE LIVE PATH IS RIGHT — SO THE FIT AND THE GAME D
open.full: every hazard lands on the side that laid it in the offline board, and the live path is right — so the fit and the game disagree. found by search 2026-08-13 while chasing #249; split out and verified independently. `engine/board.js` `notemove` ends with `if (move.sidecondition) board.startside(side, move.sidecondition, ...)` — `side` is the mover's, unconditionally. derived from the format, not recalled: of the 11 legal side-condition moves in this regulation, seven are `target: allyside` and four are `target: foeside` — stealth rock, spikes, sticky web, toxic spikes. the seven (reflect, light screen, aurora veil, safeguard, tailwind, quick guard, wide guard) are correct by accident, because the mover's side is the right answer for them. the four hazards are recorded on the layer's own side, which is the side they can never be on. this is not #249 and must not be closed with it. that row is the seed carrying no hazards into a playout — a missing feature, and a rollout that ignores hazards is merely blind. this is a feature that is present and inverted, and it sits in the board the fit reads: `engine/board.js` is the offline board, the live path reads showdown's `|-sidestart|` and gets it right. that is fitting environment and playing environment must match, broken in a new place — the same shape as mag fitted with the sheet visible and played without it, and machamp trained under broken mega. a model fitted on a board where stealth rock hurts its own team learned something about a game nobody plays. size, and it is small and that is not the argument: 259 corpus uses across the four (stealth rock 168, sticky web 42, toxic spikes 34, spikes 15) against 16,074 for tailwind alone. a wrong value is worse than a missing one at equal volume, because nothing downstream can tell it is wrong. the fix is derived, not a list of four: read `move.target` and place the condition on the far side when it is `foeside`. a hand-written hazard list here would be the ban-list-of-four shape a third time, and a hazard added next regulation would silently land on the wrong side again

open.full: 'good enough' is a usage-weighted threshold, not a row count — and by that measure the engine is already at 99.24%. will, 2026-08-10: *'we do have to ask ourelves at what point is the engine good enough and has enough used features that it can perform its end goal'*. measured against the corpus rather than argued: 553,910 total move clicks; 781 (0.14%) land on a move that resolves to a whole no-op turn; 3,888 (0.70%) land on a move the roster says disagrees with the authority; the union is 4,208 = 0.76%. so 99.24% of real clicks land on a move with no known defect, and the game differential is 150/150 clean on real replayed games. the gate is a coverage standard and has been read as a sufficiency standard. its 45 open move rows are deliberately-staged edge cases, which is precisely why they survived — they barely occur. the honest test of sufficiency is roadmap #68: scale the differential from 150 games to 1,000+ real stored games. if it stays clean there, the remaining rows are polish and can run beside search work rather than blocking it, and the #99 quarantine can lift on a measured condition instead of a feeling. note the standing counter-evidence, which cuts the same way: `docs/measure.md` §0 carries a tight null at n=8,883 on the hypothesis that correctness fixes move the leaf at all

open.title: THE OPTIMIZATION PASS — hand MEDICHAM to Fable 5 and say make it faster, but only behind a correctness gate a stopwatch
open.full: the optimization pass — hand medicham to fable 5 and say make it faster, but only behind a correctness gate a stopwatch cannot fake. will, 2026-08-10: *'once we think medicham is good enough i plan to run some optimization programs to speed it up'* / *'handing it over to feeble 5 and saying make this go faster'*. dispatchable directly — the model is selectable per agent. the hazard is that 'faster' and 'different' are indistinguishable to a benchmark. an optimizer that shaves 30% by skipping a branch produces a beautiful number and a broken engine, and every existing test can still pass because those tests cover mechanics the branch never touches. so the pass runs three instruments, not one: `tests/bench-medicham.js` for the score (built 2026-08-10, pinned fixture, best-of-5, refuses to record a baseline under load — first reading 0.4341 ms/turn); the 500-move x 4-turn whole-board digest sweep for the verdict (2,000 cells; wire 147 used it to show only 11 moved, and that is the shape every optimization must reproduce at zero); and `tests/test-damage-stages.js` at 1728/1728 exact so arithmetic shortcuts cannot drift. sequencing, which decides how much work this is: the classifier cascade is both the most likely optimization target and the thing the remaining ~20 wires append to. restructure it first and the queued fixes land in the restructured version; do the wires first and the optimizer rewrites code that was just written

open.title: THE COST OF A FEATURE DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON WHICH PATH IT SITS IN, and the first measurement of that was taken 2026-08-10.
open.full: the cost of a feature depends entirely on which path it sits in, and the first measurement of that was taken 2026-08-10. will: *'how many of these features will slow down the engine? cause if it costs nothing to have harvest in there, then sure we can, but if there is a time cost to it then maybe we otta reconsider'* — the right question, and the answer splits cleanly. hot path — runs on every click of every rollout: the damage chain and the ~40-branch classifier cascade. tonight's five wires cost +6.2% (0.776 -> 0.825 ms/turn, interleaved a/b across frozen releases under load), and the per-hit damage loop is almost certainly all of it, being the only wire that touched damage. cold path — fires once per turn on a trigger, and is effectively free: harvest, cud chew, cheek pouch, quick guard, the heal family. so harvest specifically: yes, free. the thing to actually guard is compounding — 6% per five wires, twenty more wires, and the engine is ~25% slower to serve 0.76% of clicks. that trade stops being worth it well before the queue empties, which is the argument for #76's ratchet firing on every wire rather than at the end

open.full: a few million self-play games to prove the sampler fires at the rate we declared — will's idea, and the right tool for the question it actually answers. *'once we feel our engine is good we can have it play a few million games and then determine if our rate for accuracy and secondary effects is right'*, then, on the distinction: *'correct run the million games after we determine'*. so: #132 first (is the declared number right — free, exact), then this (does the code fire at it — statistical). this catches the failure a probe structurally cannot: a probe forces the outcome to test the mechanic, so a secondary declared at 30% that a bug makes fire at 0% or 100% passes every probe and every roster row. that is claude.md's founding failure — a capability absent while everything reports success — in the one place the existing instruments are blind. cost is not a constraint: at the measured 0.4341 ms/turn and a mean 3.6-turn rollout, a million games is roughly half an hour. compare observed firing rates against the declared chances with a confidence interval per move, and expect the answer to be boring — the value is the one that is not

open.full: `data/status.js`'s graph row names the wrong builder, which is why #153 was invisible. `engine/provenance.js` attributes it to `engine/build-status.js`, which reads `policy-eval.json` and friends and is clear. the file's own header says it is generated by `build/build_status.js`, which reads two withheld artifacts — so the row that would have made `data/status.js` quarantined was never computed. two builders with almost the same name, one stale, and the graph followed the stale one. neither file may be deleted on this reasoning alone and web may not touch either; what is owed is a decision about which builder is live and a re-classification. related: `data/games.h2h-joint-trained.jsonl` and `data/games.h2h-tags2.jsonl` have no row at all, so doduo's and mew's evidence lines resolve to *unclassified* — the site withholds them on the ground that unclassified is not cleared, and that withholding expires by itself the day either file gets a row that clears.

open.full: position against three comparables, because the field is not empty and none of them is playing our game. vgc-bench (aamas 2026) — whose archive we already consume, and dropped from the fit for staleness (four days, mid-june, seven weeks old); `engine/corpus_shift.js` exists to measure the metagame distance and has never written an artifact. future sight ai — closed-source showdown bot, reportedly top 5% of the most popular format, matches revealed attributes to the most common set, ships a win-probability browser extension; also settles a naming question, since "future sight" is taken and this project names everything after pokémon. the pokeagent challenge (arxiv 2603.15563, neurips 2025, 100+ teams, two tracks) — by far the strongest reference of the three and not yet read. add sarantinos (arxiv 2212.13338, cambridge) as the closest published method: gen 7 random battles singles, peaked 33rd in the world, regret-minimisation opponent prediction, fills unknown properties from usage statistics, and explicitly rejects monte carlo sampling as too sample-inefficient — which is what miltank's leaf does. it also names our #29 independently: its first "biggest challenge" is keeping the team balanced, with a worked example that is the sack, and it asserts *"an ai agent cannot achieve this just by looking ahead with minmax or monte carlo tree search."* finally, its elo caveat is load-bearing for will's stated goal: comparing human and ai ratings is invalid unless they played each other — laddering with alakazam is exactly that, so the plan is sound and should say why
